title: An Unreliable Field

patient.name: Mr Tan Kok Leong
patient.presenting_complaint: Here for a Humphrey visual field test for glaucoma monitoring; first attempt looks unreliable

history.hpc: Mr Tan attends for an HVF (24-2) for glaucoma monitoring. During the first test he was anxious and kept pressing the button. He says: 'I think I press the button too much, scared I miss the light.' The printout shows high false positives and fixation losses. The OT must recognise the unreliable indices, re-instruct the patient, and repeat the test.
history.pmhx: Primary open-angle glaucoma, both eyes. Hypertension.
history.social_hx: Lives with wife. Compliant with drops. Non-smoker; first HVF was some time ago.

examination_findings.fundus: Glaucomatous optic discs, for doctor review with reliable fields

investigations.humphrey_visual_field: HVF 24-2 (SITA) performed. First test unreliable: high false positives and fixation losses (reliability indices flagged). The OT re-instructed the patient (respond only when a light is seen, do not guess; keep fixation on the central target), ensured correct trial lens and alignment, and repeated. The repeat showed acceptable reliability indices, allowing meaningful interpretation by the doctor.
investigations.reliability_indices: First run: high false positives and fixation losses (unreliable). Repeat: indices within acceptable limits.

diagnosis: An initially unreliable Humphrey visual field (high false positives and fixation losses) corrected by re-instruction and repetition to produce a reliable test. Reliability indices must be acceptable before a field is interpreted. The OT competency is recognising poor reliability, coaching, and repeating; interpretation of the field is the doctor's.

immediate: Check the reliability indices (fixation losses, false positives, false negatives) before accepting the test
Recognise that high false positives/fixation losses make the field unreliable
Re-instruct the patient: press only when a light is seen, do not guess, keep fixation central
Ensure the correct near trial lens is used and the eye is correctly aligned and the other eye occluded
Repeat the test and confirm the reliability indices are now acceptable
Document the test type (24-2), the reliability indices, and that a reliable result was obtained for the doctor
follow_up: Doctor to interpret the reliable field and compare with previous tests
Continue glaucoma drops and monitoring as scheduled
Note coaching needs for future tests if the patient struggles again
patient_education: Reassure him it is fine to miss some lights — he should respond only when he actually sees one
Explain not to guess or press repeatedly, and to keep looking at the central target
Explain why a reliable test matters for tracking his glaucoma
Encourage him to take short breaks if tired during the test

key_points: Identifies the patient's anxiety and button-pressing behaviour
Confirms the indication (glaucoma monitoring) and test type
Notes drop compliance and prior field tests for comparison
Explains how to perform the test correctly
Checks reliability indices (fixation losses, false positives/negatives)
Recognises the first test as unreliable rather than a true result
Ensures correct trial lens, alignment, and occlusion, then repeats
Documents test type, reliability indices, and the reliable result
Understands a field must be reliable before it can be interpreted
Knows high false positives/fixation losses indicate unreliability
Recognises re-instruction and repetition as the correct response
Knows interpretation of the field is the doctor's role
Coaches the patient effectively and repeats to obtain a reliable test
Documents the indices and reliable outcome for the doctor
Explains the test technique and reassures the patient
Notes future coaching needs if relevant
